title: Redis Caching and Redis Cloud
summary: Cache API responses with explicit serialization, expiration, and secure cloud configuration.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: How to Use Redis in Your Spring Boot Project: Step-by-Step Tutorial
Engineering Digest: How to integrate Redis Cloud with Spring Boot Application

richText: Use Redis for short-lived cached values
Redis stores values by key. A cache stores a copy that can be reused instead of calling an API or reading a database again.
A cache hit means the key has a usable value. A cache miss means the value is absent. On a miss, read the source and store the result.
TTL means time to live. A 300-second TTL expires a weather response after five minutes. Repeat requests can use the cached response during that period.
Use caching when repeated reads are expensive and briefly stale data is acceptable. Do not treat an optional cache as the only copy of a journal entry.
These examples use Spring Boot 3, Spring Framework 6, and Java 17. Add spring-boot-starter-data-redis for Redis connections and templates.
Read through a five-minute cache
StringRedisTemplate stores text keys and values with string serialization. ObjectMapper converts a Weather record to JSON and back.
Inject and reuse the Boot-managed ObjectMapper. A generic RedisTemplate declaration alone does not select JSON serialization.
The method below belongs to a service with injected redis, mapper, and provider collaborators. WeatherProvider fetches the current external weather response.
Configure the Redis Cloud connection
Use the host, port, username, and password supplied by the cloud database. Put credentials in environment variables.
This configuration assumes the provider endpoint supports TLS. TLS encrypts network traffic. Keep certificate verification enabled and use provider-supported trust settings.
Boot 3 uses the spring.data.redis prefix. Older Boot examples may use spring.redis, so check the version before copying properties.
Choose freshness and failure behavior
The first request fetches weather and stores it. A second request before expiration reads Redis. A later request after expiration fetches again.
Delete or update related keys after changing the source when stale data is unacceptable. TTL alone leaves stale values until expiration.

A connection failure differs from a miss. The snippet propagates Redis and JSON failures. For an optional cache, explicitly handle those failures and fall back to the provider without hiding them in monitoring.
Concurrent misses can call the provider more than once. Use coordination when provider limits make that unacceptable.
Include every input that changes the result in the cache key. Add user or tenant identity for private data so users cannot read each other’s cached values.
